newsitem.title: USA: U.S. High Court to hear Florida redistricting case.
newsitem.headline: U.S. High Court to hear Florida redistricting case.

text.p: The Supreme Court said Tuesday it would hear a constitutional challenge to a redistricting plan for the Florida state senate.

The plan adopted 1992 and C. Martin Lawyer and others sued, charging one of the districts in the Tampa Bay area violated the Constitution's equal protection guarantee because the boundaries had been drawn along racial lines.

After mediation, all of the parties except Lawyer reached an agreement in which the boundary lines would be modified so blacks would make up about 40 percent of the district's population, down 10 percent from the initial proposal.
Lawyer continued to object on the grounds that the boundaries still reflected an unconstitutional racial motivation.

A three-judge federal court in March approved the plan, saying it "passes any pertinent test of constitutionality and fairness." It said the district "offers to any candidate, without regard to race, the opportunity to seek elective office."

The Supreme Court, in a brief order, rejected the Justice Department's views and agreed to review the ruling. The high court will hear arguments in the case early next year, with a decision due by June.
